section: Impact of LPG on the role of the State - from provider to regulator and enabler
subsections: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state
Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment
Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift
Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s: The economic reforms initiated in 1991 shifted the Indian economy from which orientation to which orientation?
accepted.x: The 1991 crisis and the LPG reforms under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh shifted the economy from a state-controlled orientation to a market-oriented one.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of a major policy transition rather than merely recalling its year.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Who were the Prime Minister and Finance Minister associated with the initiation of the 1991 LPG reforms, respectively?
o: Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Yashwant Sinha
P.V. Narasimha Rao and Dr. Manmohan Singh
Dr. Manmohan Singh and P.V. Narasimha Rao
accepted.x: P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister and Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister when the 1991 LPG reforms were initiated.
accepted.tq: Use the person-with-policy association carefully; the offices are deliberately placed in a confusable order.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the shift from Government to Governance after the LPG reforms?
o: The State retained direct control over all services but reduced taxation.
The State transferred all regulatory powers to civil-society organisations.
The State withdrew completely from economic activity.
The State increasingly acted as facilitator, regulator and catalyst for private and civil-society participation.
accepted.x: The post-reform State moved away from being the direct provider and controller of all services and increasingly became a facilitator, regulator and catalyst for private and civil-society participation.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that captures the complete institutional shift without using an extreme claim.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Welfare or provider state — Owns and runs production
2. Regulatory state — Sets rules and uses independent regulators to police markets
3. Facilitator or enabler state — Creates conditions for private and civil-society delivery

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs correctly describe the respective roles of the welfare/provider, regulatory and facilitator/enabler states.
accepted.tq: Match each institutional model with its defining function before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: The expression “commanding heights” is associated in the Indian context with which model of the State?
accepted.x: The welfare or provider state owns and runs production, particularly the commanding heights of the economy.
accepted.tq: Test the exact phrase associated with a model rather than its general description.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 used the size of the public sector as an indicator of the extent to which the economy was:
accepted.x: Under the provider-state model, the size of the public sector was treated as a measure of how socialised the economy was.
accepted.tq: Use a look-alike conceptual option to test the exact official term.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains only instruments associated with the facilitator or enabler state?
o: Industrial licensing, MRTP controls and public-sector reservation
Capital issue control, tariff fixation and judicial review
Commanding heights, state ownership and production controls
accepted.x: Public-private partnerships, Direct Benefit Transfer, Government e-Marketplace and UMANG are instruments through which the State enables delivery by private or civil-society actors.
accepted.tq: Identify the complete cluster of instruments belonging to one State model.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s:
Which of the following represents the correct chronological order of the reforms and institutions mentioned below?

A. Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956
B. LPG reforms
C. SEBI becoming a statutory regulator
D. Establishment of TRAI
accepted.x: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 preceded the 1991 LPG reforms; SEBI acquired statutory status in 1992 and TRAI was established in 1997.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest dated policy and then place the post-1991 regulators.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Which statement best explains the change in the financial sector associated with the post-1991 shift towards a facilitator State?
o: Banks were required to obtain prior approval from the RBI for every operational decision.
The RBI began allowing banks to take decisions without consulting it in every matter, facilitating the entry of private and foreign banks.
The RBI nationalised all private and foreign banks after 1991.
The RBI ceased to regulate the banking sector altogether.
accepted.x: The reforms aimed to shift the RBI from regulator to facilitator, allowing banks greater decision-making freedom and enabling the entry of private and foreign banks. This did not mean that the RBI ceased regulation.
accepted.tq: Reject absolute interpretations of institutional change and select the precise description of delegated flexibility.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: In which sector did the State similarly move from being a direct provider to an enabler of private activity?
accepted.x: The same shift was observed in housing, where the State moved from direct provision towards enabling private real-estate activity.
accepted.tq: Test the sectoral application of the provider-to-enabler distinction.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the institutional or policy markers of the regulatory State listed in the context of post-1991 India?
o: Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 as a measure of socialisation
accepted.x: SEBI, TRAI and CERC are independent regulators associated with the regulatory State. Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956 was a marker of the welfare or provider State.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to the neighbouring State model rather than the regulatory model.
accepted.sec: State roles compared - welfare, regulatory, facilitator/enabler state

accepted.s: Industrial licensing was abolished in the reform period except for which of the following groups of industries?
o: Alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace and drugs or pharmaceuticals
Banking, insurance, telecom, railways, ports, roads and aviation
Textiles, automobiles, cement, sugar, paper, electronics and fertilisers
Agriculture, fisheries, handicrafts, retail trade, tourism, education and health
accepted.x: The exempted categories included alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace and drugs or pharmaceuticals.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete exception list; distractors substitute ordinary industries for the specified reserved categories.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: The number of industries reserved for the public sector changed in which sequence?
accepted.x: The public-sector reservation list was reduced in phases from 17 industries under Schedule A in 1956 to 8 in 1991 and later to 3.
accepted.tq: Track the direction and stages of numerical reduction instead of treating the figures as isolated facts.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: Which development contributed to the opening of defence production to the private sector in 2001?
o: The opening of defence production to private participation
The abolition of the MRTP Act asset limits
accepted.x: Defence production was opened to the private sector in 2001, which affected the composition of the public-sector reservation list.
accepted.tq: Link a dated policy change with its direct effect on a reservation list.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding goods reserved for small-scale industries is correct?
o: They remained permanently reserved for small-scale industries.
They were transferred exclusively to the public sector in 2015.
They were newly reserved after 1991, with the last items reserved in 2015.
They were progressively de-reserved, and the last items were de-reserved in 2015.
accepted.x: Goods reserved for small-scale industries were progressively de-reserved, and the last items were de-reserved in 2015.
accepted.tq: Watch the reversed policy direction: de-reservation, not expansion of reservation, is the correct trend.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: The abolition of asset limits under the MRTP Act removed restrictions relating to which set of activities?
o: Tax collection, monetary policy, public expenditure and budgeting
Citizens’ Charters, RTI, DBT and e-governance
Agricultural land ownership, tenancy and irrigation
Concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions
accepted.x: Abolition of MRTP asset limits removed curbs on concentration, entry, expansion, mergers and acquisitions.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the complete policy-effect cluster associated with the MRTP change.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: Public sector enterprises were given greater autonomy through which of the following measures?
o: Transfer of all PSUs to local governments
Industrial licensing and compulsory state ownership
MoUs and Navratna or Maharatna status
accepted.x: Public sector enterprises received greater autonomy through Memoranda of Understanding and Navratna or Maharatna status.
accepted.tq: Use the exact institutional instruments rather than a broad but inaccurate description of autonomy.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: Disinvestment in India began in 1991–92 with an initial target of:
accepted.x: Disinvestment began in 1991–92 with a target of ₹2,500 crore. Initially, the objective was to bridge the fiscal deficit, and later efficiency improvement was also emphasised.
accepted.tq: Test the exact inaugural target using closely spaced monetary distractors.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: Which of the following was a criticism of the disinvestment process?
o: The proceeds were used exclusively for expanding social infrastructure.
PSU assets were consistently overvalued and no fiscal purpose was served.
Disinvestment prevented all private participation in public enterprises.
PSU assets were undervalued and the proceeds were used to plug revenue gaps rather than develop PSUs or social infrastructure.
accepted.x: A major criticism was that PSU assets were undervalued and disinvestment proceeds were used to fill revenue gaps instead of funding PSU development or social infrastructure.
accepted.tq: Identify the criticism containing both the valuation issue and the use-of-proceeds issue.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: As of August 2026, the amount raised in 2026–27 through stake sales in seven PSUs along with SUUTI remittances was:
accepted.x: ₹21,082 crore had been raised in 2026–27 through stake sales in seven PSUs together with SUUTI remittances, as of August 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise current-affairs figure from nearby monetary values.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: SEBI granted LIC time up to which date to reach the 10% minimum public shareholding requirement?
accepted.x: SEBI granted LIC time until 16 May 2027 to achieve the 10% minimum public shareholding requirement.
accepted.tq: Check both the day-month and year in a time-limit question.
accepted.sec: Rolling back the State - public sector reservation list, disinvestment

accepted.s: Which regulator was established under the SEBI Act, 1992 and replaced the Controller of Capital Issues?
accepted.x: SEBI became a statutory regulator under the SEBI Act, 1992 and replaced the Controller of Capital Issues in the securities market.
accepted.tq: Apply the who-replaced-whom trap to distinguish regulators with similar economic functions.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Regulator)
A. SEBI
B. TRAI
C. CERC
D. IRDA

List-II (Sector)
I. Insurance
II. Telecom
III. Power tariffs and inter-state transmission
IV. Securities market

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: SEBI regulates the securities market, TRAI telecom, CERC power tariffs and inter-state transmission, and IRDA insurance.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure regulator-sector pairs and eliminate codes that reverse the institutional domains.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. TRAI was established in 1997 under the TRAI Act, 1997.
2. CERC was established in 1998 under the Electricity Regulatory Commissions Act, 1998.
3. CERC now functions under the Electricity Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. TRAI dates from 1997, CERC from 1998, and CERC now operates under the Electricity Act, 2003.
accepted.tq: Verify each regulator against both its establishing law and its later legal basis.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: TRAI was established under the TRAI Act, 1997. The Competition Act, 2002 established the framework for CCI and replaced the MRTP Act.
accepted.tq: Use the statute-body association and identify the swapped legislation.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct description of the sector regulated by PNGRB?
accepted.x: PNGRB, established under the PNGRB Act, 2006, regulates the petroleum and gas pipeline sector.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between regulators by sector, especially where energy-related bodies appear similar.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s: Under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, which body administers the scheme and which body regulates carbon trading, respectively?
accepted.x: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency administers the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, while CERC regulates carbon trading under the scheme.
accepted.tq: Separate the administering body from the regulating body instead of assuming they are the same.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s: The TV Ratings Policy 2026 made which authority the sole authority over television rating agencies?
accepted.x: The TV Ratings Policy 2026 made the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting the sole authority over television rating agencies, ending the overlap with TRAI.
accepted.tq: Test the recent transfer of authority and avoid the familiar-but-displaced regulator trap.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Economic Survey 2025–26:
1. Regulators exercise legislative, executive and judicial powers.
2. It recommended balancing regulatory independence with accountability.
3. It proposed dedicated regulatory careers for younger professionals instead of relying mainly on retired bureaucrats.
4. It suggested statutory timelines for clearances, with penalties for delay.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Economic Survey made all four recommendations or observations: regulators exercise multiple kinds of powers, independence must be balanced with accountability, younger professionals should have dedicated regulatory careers, and delayed clearances should attract penalties.
accepted.tq: Treat each reform recommendation as an independent statement and check the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s: Which group of regulators was specifically noted as moving from reactive to anticipatory governance?
accepted.x: The Economic Survey noted that RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA were moving from reactive to anticipatory governance.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete institutional grouping rather than selecting a partly familiar list.
accepted.sec: Independent regulators after 1991 (SEBI, TRAI, CERC) as a governance shift

accepted.s: The slogan “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” dates from:
accepted.x: The slogan “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance” dates from 2014.
accepted.tq: Use the closest policy-era dates as distractors and identify the slogan’s stated origin year.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s: Which of the following best expresses the meaning of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance”?
o: A leaner State that does less itself but governs better through rules, technology and accountability
A State that directly provides every service through public enterprises
A State that withdraws from all regulation and public accountability
A State that replaces all public institutions with private companies
accepted.x: The expression refers to a leaner State that performs fewer activities directly but governs more effectively through rules, technology and accountability.
accepted.tq: Reject extreme interpretations of “minimum government” and select the balanced meaning.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s: The Right to Information Act, 2005 is associated with ending which administrative culture?
accepted.x: The RTI Act, 2005 is described as ending the colonial culture of official secrecy.
accepted.tq: Associate a landmark statute with its stated governance effect.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s: Citizens’ Charters primarily provide for:
accepted.x: Citizens’ Charters specify service standards and provide a framework for grievance redressal.
accepted.tq: Identify the citizen-facing accountability instrument by its core functions.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with its governance function?

1. Aadhaar, DBT, GeM and UMANG — E-governance
2. Performance auditing — NPM technique
3. Contracting out non-core services — NPM technique
4. Treating the citizen as a customer — NPM technique

Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four are correctly matched. The listed digital platforms are e-governance instruments, while performance auditing, contracting out non-core services and the citizen-as-customer approach are NPM techniques.
accepted.tq: Classify each instrument by whether it belongs to e-governance or New Public Management.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an instrument associated with e-governance for reducing discretion and middlemen?
accepted.x: Aadhaar, DBT and GeM are e-governance instruments that can reduce discretion and middlemen. Navratna status concerns autonomy for public sector enterprises, not e-governance.
accepted.tq: Separate digital governance tools from public-enterprise autonomy measures.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments

accepted.s: Which combination represents the capacity and administrative reform dimension of “Minimum Government, Maximum Governance”?
o: Expansion of industrial licensing and public-sector reservation
Capacity building and right-sizing of the bureaucracy
Replacement of grievance redressal with official secrecy
accepted.x: Capacity building and right-sizing of the bureaucracy are administrative measures intended to support leaner and more effective governance.
accepted.tq: Identify the positive reform pair and reject options that reverse the governance objective.
accepted.sec: Minimum Government, Maximum Governance - meaning and instruments
